                    ### Question
                    A 36-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-week history of progressively worsening pain on the outer side of her left elbow. She does not recall any trauma to the area. The patient plays badminton recreationally. Examination shows tenderness over the lateral surface of the left distal humerus. The pain is reproduced by supinating the forearm against resistance. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's pain?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Excessive stress to bone
opb. Nerve compression at the elbow
opc. Bursal inflammation
opd. Repeated wrist extension
ope. Repeated wrist flexion

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The most likely underlying cause of this patient's pain is lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow) due to repetitive supination against resistance. This condition is characterized by pain on the outer side of the elbow and is not directly related to excessive stress to the bone, nerve compression at the elbow, bursal inflammation, repeated wrist extension, or repeated wrist flexion.
